name: desire for social influence
description: Wanting to influence others in how they perceive the world.

variations.name: desire to teach
variations.description: If you see a gap in understanding and want to be a part of the solution, sharing ideas with others can legitimately help them.

variations.name: desire to control others
variations.description: If you plan to penalize people who don't fall under your influence, this is social control.

variations.name: desire to make your mark
variations.description: Influence can include non-verbal impact, like wanting to be the one to track up a fresh snowfall.

variations.name: desire to annoy
variations.description: Influence can mean having a negative impact on some social group, ranging from graffiti to terrorists. In this case, there's probably a trade for negative attention from one group bring positive attention from another.

commentaries.quote: Of course people often want things for multiple reasons. There's no harm in helping others while also hoping for a favorable response.
If you're aiming to help others who are perceived as likely to make poor choices on their own, it may be perceived as 'preachy'.

conditions: Perception that other agents need help with information or in making good choices.

1.description: Whether you're helping someone or receiving positive feedback, it likely releases reward chemicals in your brain.
